newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends up on fund influx, export moves.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends up on fund influx, export moves.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed higher against its American counterpart on Monday on foreign fund inflows and exporters' U.S. dollar sales, dealers said.
The local dollar ended at T$27.471 against Saturday's T$27.482 finish.
Turnover through dealers was a heavy US$347.5 million.
Dealers noted active U.S. dollar sales by exporters.

"Several banks have predicted a Taiwan dollar uptrend due to a rising trade surplus and corporate funding needs near the Chinese new year (on February 7)," said one dealer. "Exporters, therefore, actively entered to dump the greenback."
Dealers also saw rising inflows of foreign funds for the surging stock market in recent sessions.
"Many analysts had forecast a sound outlook for the 1997 domestic stock market, so increasing foreign fund inflows should not be a surprise," said another dealer.
But dealers said they saw now sharp Taiwan dollar appreciation ahead.
"A firming trend (for the Taiwan dollar) to test T$27.45 is a more appropriate prediction," said one dealer.
A T$27.46-27.48 range was seen for Tuesday.
